scope: Read-only inspection of Behera guarded adapter, isolated tests, actual canonical target paths, approval design and reused Aranadan transaction engine; no real installation was run.
passes: Root approval pins all eight target roles, every approved asset, the adapter and the reused engine before clean installation.

The source's 6864 rows and their accepted audit union are closed against the approved key set; existing legacy keys, unrelated registry rows and bibliography entries have explicit preservation guards.
The staged journal validates asset hashes and restricts partial targets to the approved baseline or approved output. A complete receipt is validated on re-entry.
Rollback rechecks staged output or original baseline for every target, restores only approved backups, and refuses intervening edits.
Fixture tests cover missing approval, forged journal stage, partial recovery, no-op receipt, rollback and unrelated metadata changes; the real workspace has no acceptance manifest yet.

material_issue.location: After the target replacement loop and before installation-receipt.json is written
material_issue.finding: Only durable identity is rehashed. Previously written shared targets are not rehashed before the complete receipt is published. A concurrent edit to bibliography or registries after replacement of that target, while later targets are written, can result in a false success receipt. A later invocation detects drift, but the initial installation claims completion incorrectly.
material_issue.recommendation: Assert file_hash(path) == digest(content) for every planned target immediately before the receipt write. Add a synthetic interruption/drift fixture. This changes the shared engine, so the exact new engine hash must be approved in root-acceptance.json.

deferred: No final approved Behera asset set or root-acceptance.json exists yet; current real-target checks are design-level rather than final-baseline-value checks.
No full multi-source CLDF build, durable-ID graph parity or browser QA was run.
